The United States moved to force the divestiture or ban of TikTok due to national-security concerns, specifically the potential for Chinese government access to US user data and the platform's algorithm [Source: ev-1].

Legislatively, President Biden signed the Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act on 2024-04-24, mandating that ByteDance divest TikTok’s US operations within roughly 270 days (extendable by an additional 90 days) or face a ban [Source: ev-1].

No, text says 'one day before the effective date'. [Source: ev-1]

TikTok went dark... [Source: ev-1]

on 2025.01.18/19 and was restored 2025.01.19 after President Trump pledged to pause enforcement; his executive order of 2025.01.20 delayed enforcement for 75 days.' The text implies the threat/ban took effect around Jan 18-19, 2025.] [Source: ev-1].

The dispute was ultimately resolved through an Oracle-led deal announced on 2025.06.10 [Source: ev-1].

Under this agreement, which Vice President JD Vance helped negotiate at the White House level, Oracle acquired approximately a 12.5% stake in TikTok’s US operations, with participation from SoftBank and other investors [Source: ev-1].
